title: Ge/YbF3 Dual-Cavity Defect Filter with Exact 22-Layer Count
scientific_hypothesis: A dual-cavity defect structure using high-index Ge and low-index YbF3 can simultaneously transmit two narrow bands (3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm) while blocking adjacent regions, with cavity positions and thicknesses optimized under TMM.
design_principle: Two resonant cavities separated by distributed Bragg reflector sections, each cavity tuned to one passband center wavelength via defect layer thickness. Quarter-wave stack mirrors provide out-of-band blocking.
proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/YbF3]_4 | Ge_defect1 | [YbF3/Ge]_3 | YbF3_defect2 | [Ge/YbF3]_4 | CaF2 substrate. Total finite layers: 22 (8 mirror pairs + 2 defect layers).
design_variables: Defect layer positions fixed at layers 9 and 16
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count exactly 22, within 24-layer limit
Ge and YbF3 are conventional IR dielectrics with established deposition processes
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for Bragg mirrors
Defect cavity resonance theory for narrow passbands
expected_advantages: High index contrast (Ge ~4.0, YbF3 ~1.5) enables strong blocking with fewer layers
Dual-cavity design naturally supports two independent passbands
known_risks: Ge has absorption in mid-IR that may reduce peak transmittance
Cavity coupling may cause passband interaction if spacing is incorrect
Previous route_03 failed due to layer count mismatch - this route explicitly declares 22 layers
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer stack on CaF2 substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: Layer1=Ge, Layer2=YbF3, Layer3=Ge, Layer4=YbF3, Layer5=Ge, Layer6=YbF3, Layer7=Ge, Layer8=YbF3, Layer9=Ge(defect1), Layer10=YbF3, Layer11=Ge, Layer12=YbF3, Layer13=Ge, Layer14=YbF3, Layer15=Ge, Layer16=YbF3(defect2), Layer17=Ge, Layer18=YbF3, Layer19=Ge, Layer20=YbF3, Layer21=Ge, Layer22=YbF3. All thicknesses bounded [300, 1500] nm. Optimize for: maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm, maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm, minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm, minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm. Use TMM solver with normal incidence, unpolarized light. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
revision_reason: Previous route_03 failed compilation due to layer count mismatch (declared 20, actual 21). This route explicitly declares exactly 22 layers in both topology description and execution request to prevent mismatch. Material pair Ge/YbF3 retained from prior attempt but with corrected layer count and expanded thickness bounds [300, 1500] nm to ensure geometric feasibility.
